title: a loose comparison of a non-numeric string with 0 is always false since PHP 8

ground_truth.statement: Since PHP 8 an int compared to a non-numeric string is compared as a string, so 'abc' == 0 is false; the branch is unreachable. PHP 7 converted the string to a number, which made the same comparison true - the legacy code kept its meaning only while the language did.

allowed.reason: The guarded body is unreachable for the same reason; a second correct report about the same comparison is not a false positive.
Mago reports the same site twice, once for the comparison and once for the resulting condition. The second diagnostic is correct, not noise.

notes: PHPStan 2.3.1 (equal.alwaysFalse) and Mago 1.57.0 (redundant-comparison) report the comparison as constant; Psalm 6.20.0 is silent for this operand pair, although it reports TypeDoesNotContainType for a loose comparison between two non-numeric literals and for two int literals, so the silence is a local gap rather than a different rule class. The citation is the comparison-operators page, whose type-juggling table defines the PHP 8 rule; runtime/check.php evaluates the comparison in the running PHP.
